s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual impairment with night blindness and peripheral vision loss
salient_findings: Night blindness since childhood
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field
Abnormal electroretinogram (ERG) with flat rod response
Hypofluorescence on fundus autofluorescence
Inner retinal thickening and disorganization on optical coherence tomography (OCT)
key_facts: Patient age 42
Symptoms started in childhood
Night blindness is the only symptom reported by the patient
Visual acuity 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes
Color vision is normal
Fundus examination shows few yellow spots and an indistinct grayish circle
ERG shows large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
ERG shows flat rod response
Fundus autofluorescence shows hypofluorescence in superotemporal zones
OCT shows supernormal thickness in perifoveal region
OCT shows marked inner retinal thickening and disorganization in eccentric areas
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

shortlist.label: Goldmann-Favre Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and specific ERG and fundus autofluorescence findings

shortlist.label: Congenital Stationary Night Blindness
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with night blindness since childhood and normal visual acuity, but less specific ERG findings

shortlist.label: Enhanced S-cone syndrome (ESCS)
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain night blindness and specific ERG findings, but less common and requires further differentiation

shortlist.label: Retinitis Pigmentosa
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents with progressive visual impairment and night blindness, but often with more pronounced pigmentary degeneration

shortlist.label: Leber Congenital Amaurosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although severe visual impairment is typical, some forms may present with night blindness and less severe visual acuity loss

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of night blindness since childhood, normal color vision, and specific findings on ERG, fundus autofluorescence, and OCT are consistent with Goldmann-Favre Syndrome, which is characterized by night blindness, often with a relatively preserved visual acuity and specific retinal changes.

rejected.label: Congenital Stationary Night Blindness
rejected.why: Lack of progression and specific retinal changes do not fully match the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Enhanced S-cone syndrome (ESCS)
rejected.why: Typically presents with more significant visual acuity loss and different retinal findings

rejected.label: Retinitis Pigmentosa
rejected.why: Usually presents with more widespread retinal degeneration and pigmentary changes not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Leber Congenital Amaurosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with severe visual impairment from birth, which does not match the patient's relatively preserved visual acuity
